value_features.logical_semantics: Fixed arrays preserve element order, declared length, indexing, projection, argument, and return behavior.
Boolean values preserve truth, equality, condition, argument, and return behavior.
Enum values preserve variant identity, payload meaning, construction, matching, argument, and return behavior.
Maps preserve key equality, replacement, lookup, containment, key enumeration, and missing-key behavior.
Numeric values preserve declared width, signedness, arithmetic, comparison, conversion, argument, and return behavior.
Optional values preserve present or absent identity, payload meaning, matching, argument, and return behavior.
Owned values preserve move, use-after-move rejection, argument transfer, and return ownership behavior.
Outcome values preserve success or error identity, payload meaning, matching, propagation, argument, and return behavior.
Borrowed slices preserve bounded views, element order, length, indexing, and aliasing behavior.
Strings preserve Unicode text, byte-length, comparison, concatenation, slicing helpers, argument, and return behavior.
Structured values preserve named field identity, construction, projection, argument, and return behavior.
Tuples preserve positional identity, element order, construction, projection, argument, and return behavior.

capability_shims.logical_semantics: Asynchronous operations require declared async authority and preserve readiness, joining, cancellation, timeout, channel, and selection behavior.
Clock operations require declared clock authority and preserve time observation, elapsed duration, and bounded sleep behavior.
Authenticated encryption requires declared crypto authority and preserves algorithm, key, nonce, associated-data, ciphertext, and authentication behavior.
Hash operations require declared crypto authority and preserve algorithm, input, digest, and verification behavior.
Message authentication requires declared crypto authority and preserves algorithm, key, message, tag, and verification behavior.
Random operations require declared crypto authority and preserve bounded byte generation and unsigned scalar generation behavior.

Signature operations require declared crypto authority. Ed25519 signing accepts exactly the canonical 32-byte private seed and rejects the former 64-byte seed-plus-public-key input; key generation returns the 32-byte seed and verification preserves public-key, message, signature, and boolean behavior.
Environment reads require declared environment authority and preserve allowlist, present, absent, and secret-safe audit behavior.
Foreign calls require declared foreign-call authority and preserve library, symbol, argument, result, denial, and audit behavior.
Filesystem reads require declared read authority and preserve scoped path, bytes, text, absence, denial, and audit behavior.
Filesystem writes require declared write authority and preserve scoped path, content, replacement, denial, and audit behavior.
Standard input, output, error, and logging preserve byte, text, line, flush, and redaction behavior.
Structured-data operations preserve null, boolean, integer, text, array, object, parse, field, item, stringify, and error behavior.
Name resolution requires declared network authority and preserves host, address, denial, and error behavior.
Asynchronous HTTP serving requires declared async authority and preserves request, response, cancellation, draining, denial, and error behavior.
HTTP requests require declared network authority and preserve method, URL, headers, body, response, cancellation, denial, and error behavior.
HTTP serving requires declared network authority and preserves binding, request, response, backpressure, draining, denial, and error behavior.
TCP operations require declared network authority and preserve address, connection, ordered bytes, closure, denial, and error behavior.
UDP operations require declared network authority and preserve address, datagram boundaries, denial, and error behavior.
Process execution requires declared process authority and preserves command policy, normalized status, absence, denial, and audit behavior.
Pattern operations preserve compilation, matching, capture, replacement, and invalid-pattern behavior.
Synchronization operations preserve mutual exclusion, shared access, notification, ordering, poisoning, and shutdown behavior.
